title: arXiv Physics — Daily notable papers (11 November 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper ordering based on limited editorial curation, cross-listing, concrete results and methods, and other checkable signals. Citation evidence is limited for papers this new, so the ordering does not establish popularity.

sections.title: First constraints on axion-like particles with SPHEREx data
sections.abstract: Using 16.5 months of SPHEREx near-infrared data, the authors set new limits on axion-like dark matter over 0.496–3.32 eV and find substantial headroom for improving sensitivity through analysis methods.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a 95% power-constrained upper limit as strong as g_agamma < 2.10e-11 GeV^-1 at m_a = 0.606 eV, with median lifetime limit tau > 6.5e25 s; they find no unknown high-significance line.
sections.evidence_type: observational; analysis of 16.5 months of SPHEREx QR2/QR3 data from the North and South Deep Fields
sections.unique_caveat: The limit assumes an NFW Milky Way halo and a specified dark-matter velocity dispersion; masking and known spectral features reduce sensitivity, and the authors estimate methodological improvements could strengthen limits by over an order of magnitude.
sections.ranking_evidence: First ALP search with SPHEREx observations, two-archive relevance, numerical coupling and lifetime limits, and a public analysis-code link reported in the paper.

sections.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: A 63-qubit superconducting processor simulates string evolution in a two-dimensional Z2 gauge theory, resolving charge and flux spreading, pair creation, and transverse string rearrangement across confined and deconfined regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report rapid charge/flux spreading in the deconfined regime, stronger matter occupation near the pair-creation resonance, and suppression of spreading at strong electric fields.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; digital quantum simulation on 63 superconducting qubits, checked with ancilla and gauge-constraint measurements and noise rescaling
sections.unique_caveat: The simulated evolution is finite-depth and noise-mitigated; classical PEPS comparisons are considered converged only over limited time windows, and later-time hardware data have larger uncertainties.
sections.ranking_evidence: A concrete many-qubit experiment reports 12 ancillas, up to 15 second-order Trotter steps, and direct access to local Gauss-law constraints as an error-detection resource.

sections.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
sections.abstract: The authors propose a fast-scrambling-time correction to the cosmological Raychaudhuri equation, derive background solutions and proxy constraints, and show how neutrino mass transitions could leave a residual dark-energy contribution.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain proxy estimates Gamma = -3.7 +/- 6.1 from BBN and Gamma approximately -2.8 +/- 0.9 by translating existing CMB/BAO/supernova fits, with a history-dependent dark-energy term of order sigma m_nu^4 when neutrinos become non-relativistic.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; modified-FLRW background equations, analytic solutions, and proxy constraints translated from existing cosmological fits
sections.unique_caveat: This is a phenomenological, background-level model rather than an observational detection; the authors call for a dedicated likelihood analysis and a consistent treatment of structure formation and perturbations.
sections.ranking_evidence: Highlighted in an independent 11 November arXiv digest and cross-listed across cosmology, gravitation, and high-energy theory; it provides explicit proxy bounds and a route to a full likelihood analysis.

sections.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes
sections.abstract: A coronal stochastic-acceleration model is used to forecast detection prospects for nearby Seyfert galaxies with a joint IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE network, favoring Circinus as a point-source target and X-ray-informed stacking for other sources.
sections.claimed_result: The authors forecast a 5sigma Circinus detection by 2038 at the latest only if Seyferts supply the diffuse neutrino flux up to 100 TeV and Circinus is at least as efficient as the population average.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; model-based point-source and stacking sensitivity estimates for IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE
sections.unique_caveat: The timeline depends on the assumed Seyfert contribution and Circinus efficiency; the paper does not report a new neutrino detection, and it expects other individual sources to remain difficult.
sections.ranking_evidence: Featured in the independent 11 November arXiv digest; it combines four neutrino facilities with an explicit source-emission model and a conditional detection forecast.

sections.title: Theory overview on LLP searches at the LHC
sections.abstract: These proceedings review heavy neutral leptons as long-lived-particle benchmarks, comparing displaced signatures in the minimal active–sterile mixing scenario with signatures opened by additional interactions.
sections.claimed_result: The author argues that additional HNL interactions can modify production and decay mechanisms and create search signatures beyond the mixing-only benchmark.
sections.evidence_type: review; proceedings overview of HNL long-lived-particle phenomenology and LHC search strategies
sections.unique_caveat: This is a compact overview, not a new collider analysis or a measured HNL signal; its conclusions depend on which non-minimal interactions are realized.
sections.ranking_evidence: The lead item in an independent 11 November arXiv digest; the proceedings connect minimal and extended HNL models to distinct LHC production, decay, and displaced-signature searches.

sections.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
sections.abstract: The authors numerically solve the SU(2) BFSS ground state and use its wavefunction and finite-box spectra to extract scattering amplitudes, positive-energy bound states, and metastable resonances.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the expected Born–Oppenheimer v^4/r^7 interaction in the appropriate regime and identify positive-energy bound states in several SO(9) irreducible representations plus metastable resonances.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerical solution of the SU(2) matrix quantum mechanics, matrix-bootstrap comparisons, and Lüscher finite-box scattering analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The study is restricted to SU(2), not the large-N holographic regime; extracting observables requires tail fits and finite-box corrections, and the authors note that larger N will be substantially harder numerically.
sections.ranking_evidence: Ground-state correlators agree with independent matrix-bootstrap islands to about five significant figures, while the three-point amplitude agrees with a prior computation; the paper also reports a nonperturbative four-point extraction.

sections.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate a visible/near-UV thin-film lithium-niobate platform integrating couplers, beamsplitters, resonators, and modulators, with modulation bandwidth beyond 50 GHz at 493 nm.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report segmented traveling-wave modulators with a 450 mV·cm half-wave voltage–length product and >20 dB extinction, alongside ring resonators with 2.9 ± 0.2 dB/cm propagation loss.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; integrated photonic device fabrication and optical characterization at 493 nm
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify photorefraction and substrate uniformity as obstacles to scaling the platform.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper reports measured device-level metrics at a wavelength relevant to trapped-ion systems, including >50 GHz bandwidth and resonator loss; it combines several photonic components on one platform.

sections.title: Type IIB instanton corrections from pure modular unfolding
sections.abstract: The paper develops a modular-symmetry method to reconstruct higher Fourier modes of type-IIB interaction coefficients from low-mode data, without using supersymmetry differential equations.
sections.claimed_result: The author reconstructs higher modes for the D6R4 coefficient and derives the g_s^-1/2 and constant weak-coupling instanton-prefactor terms at each fixed positive charge, matching the known expansion.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; modular spectral analysis of type-IIB higher-derivative interaction coefficients
sections.unique_caveat: Extracting cusp amplitudes assumes the conjectured simplicity of the even cusp spectrum and complete low-mode data; the paper identifies additional information needed for higher-charge D8R4 predictions.
sections.ranking_evidence: Featured as a technical highlight in the independent 11 November arXiv digest; the work combines Rankin–Selberg unfolding, Hecke relations, the Kuznetsov trace formula, and spectral-tail bounds.

sections.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
sections.abstract: A renormalization-group treatment is used to connect galaxy-bias parameters measured at finite field-level cutoffs to low-k n-point-function measurements, with tests on perturbative mocks and N-body halo catalogues.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that the RG-predicted running of bias parameters matches measurements across cutoffs and approaches the tree-level n-point estimates as the cutoff tends to zero.
sections.evidence_type: computational; forward-model galaxy fields and halo catalogues from full N-body simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated connection is established on model-generated fields and halo catalogues; applying it to survey data requires controlling the bias-expansion and simulation systematics.
sections.ranking_evidence: The same RG prediction is tested against both Lagrangian-perturbation mock fields and full N-body halo catalogues, bridging two cosmological-analysis schemes.

sections.title: Chiral Superconductivity Indifferent to Parent Topology in the Square-Lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard Model
sections.abstract: DMRG, finite-temperature DQMC, parton analysis, and weak-coupling calculations indicate that doping several distinct phases of a pi-flux Hofstadter–Hubbard model produces the same chiral topological superconducting state.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a chiral topological superconductor with spin Chern number -2 across nearly the full doped phase diagram, independent of whether the parent state is IQH, chiral-spin-liquid, or antiferromagnetic.
sections.evidence_type: computational; DMRG, finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo, parton analysis, and weak-coupling perturbation theory
sections.unique_caveat: This is a result for a proposed lattice model, not an observation of superconductivity in a material; the predicted phase diagram depends on the model and numerical regimes studied.
sections.ranking_evidence: Several complementary methods—DMRG, DQMC, parton analysis, and perturbation theory—support the result, which is cross-listed in strongly correlated electrons and superconductivity.

sections.title: Planckian Charge Equilibration in Fast Scramblers
sections.abstract: Linear-response calculations for maximally scrambling complex SYK and Yukawa models yield a Planckian slow charge-imbalance relaxation rate whose dimensionless prefactor depends on the fermion scaling dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive Gamma = 2pi(2Delta - d)kBT/hbar for the slowest relative-charge mode and show that maximal scrambling does not determine its dimensionless prefactor.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; conformal linear-response analysis and numerical real-time Green-function calculations for d = 0 and d = 1 models
sections.unique_caveat: The result applies to the studied conformal models; the authors leave the conserved center-charge response and its possible ballistic-to-diffusive crossover unresolved.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed between strongly correlated electrons and high-energy theory; combines an analytic conformal-regime expression with numerical checks in SYK and Yukawa models.

sections.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
sections.abstract: A custom IFIC setup measures angle-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet reflectance from rough metal samples across 128–500 nm to support optical modeling of noble-element scintillation detectors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use angular BRDF measurements and a GGX microfacet fit to infer refractive-index and roughness parameters for aluminum and stainless steel, then extrapolate reflectance to liquid argon and xenon.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; monochromator-based, angle-resolved reflectance measurements in gaseous argon
sections.unique_caveat: Hemispherical reflectance in liquid media is extrapolated from in-plane measurements using a surface-scattering model, rather than measured directly throughout the liquid hemisphere.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work addresses scarce reflectance data at argon and xenon scintillation wavelengths, reports a characterized instrument over a broad VUV band, and is cross-listed in detector physics, high-energy experiment, and optics.

sections.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
sections.abstract: In a cold weakly ionized laboratory plasma, time-resolved ion measurements show hydrated negative-ion clusters growing as water ice begins to form below about 200 K.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that ice grains appear only with ionization, alongside growth and then a sharp abundance drop of hydrated negative ions, consistent with rapid conversion into macroscopic grains below a critical temperature.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; cold weakly ionized plasma with trace water and time-resolved ion mass spectrometry
sections.unique_caveat: The authors’ application to mesospheres and protoplanetary disks is an environmental analogy; dominance over dust-surface deposition depends on sufficient UV, low temperature, and negative-ion production.
sections.ranking_evidence: A laboratory result is cross-listed across exoplanetary science, plasma physics, and space physics; it reports time-resolved ion-cluster measurements and a contrast with the non-ionized control.
